lessons.title: What is an AIOS?
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
An AIOS is an operating system for how you run the business with agents, and I want to be precise, because the phrase gets used for a chatbot with a folder next to it.
Windows runs the computer. Your AIOS runs the work. It is not a clever prompt you saved, and it is not another forty-nine-dollar tab you open twice. It is your context, your numbers, your meetings, the jobs you actually repeat, and the builds you keep — five plates, one thread through them.
What that looks like when it is running
It knows the business, so you stop re-explaining yourself every chat.
It can see the numbers you actually use, not seven dashboards you assemble in your head.
It watches the meetings and the messages and puts a brief where you will read it.
It lives in the harness you already open — Claude, Cursor, Codex, or Grok Bot.
It does the repeatable jobs so your hours go back to the work that moves something.
Fifteen modules. After every one you type
/aios
and it asks where you are — empty, halfway, or already running — and which lesson you are in. That is the gold thread on the cover.
I run NavAIgate, BluPlai and this classroom on that shape. Chief of Staff 0.4.2 is the crew. Design Brain is 1,119 sourced entries. The chart gallery is 19 charts you actually open. My voice file, my brain search and my invoices stay on my machines. You will build yours.
Type
/aios
and tell it you just finished what an AIOS is.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: The Operator Trap
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
You started a business to be free, and then somewhere along the way it inverted. You check dashboards before you have finished your coffee, and you sit in meetings whose only job is to keep you across things, and you have quietly become the highest-paid administrator in your own company.
That is the operator trap. You are the integration layer. Every tool dumps a job back on you, and you call that being across it.
We are not going to hire three people to manage the chaos, and we are not going to collect a drawer of downloads and call it a system. Context, numbers, meetings, tasks and builds sit on five plates, and a crew runs the repeatable bits.
If you recognise the Tuesday morning, stay on the path. If your week is already a system and you are only missing one plate, type
/aios
, say already running, and we fill the gap. We do not wipe a working desk to make a clean demo.
Type
/aios
when you have named the trap in your own week — one sentence is enough.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Five layers, four harnesses
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Look at the cover. Annual only. Your AIOS. Five layers — Context, Data, Intelligence, Automate, Build — and along the bottom, Grok Bot, Claude, Cursor, Codex.
The plates are the course. The icons are how you drive it. Call 55 was the whole point: the harness does not matter, the approach does.
The five plates
Context
— the machine knows the business. Your rules, your voice start, git if you already have it.
Data
— numbers you can actually ask, from your sources.
Intelligence
— meetings, the brief, Grok Bot in your pocket. Hermes if you like tinkering.
Automate
— a task audit of what you really do, then automate that.
Build
— architect what is left after the first four plates.
After those five, we put Design Brain, the 19-chart gallery, and the lesson where you build your voice, your memory and your invoices. Content Coach and Hormozi sit at the end because that is what we actually run in Inner Circle.
Type
/aios
and say which harness you will use for the next plate.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: /aios — where are you
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Alright. Before we put anything on the five layers, we look at the folder you already have, because most of you are not starting from nothing, and I am not going to wipe a messy project to make a clean demo.
Type
/aios
in the harness you actually use and answer the two questions. It asks them at the start, and it asks them again after every layer, and that is deliberate.
Question 1 — where is the machine
Empty.
New folder. We start at layer 1 and we do not skip.
Halfway.
Notes, a half-written CLAUDE.md, a few abandoned folders. We do not delete that. We name what is already there and we fill the gap.
Already running.
You have a crew, or a voice, or a daily brief. We run status first. Then we only add the missing plate.
Question 2 — which lesson are you in
Your AIOS, Useful Resources, a recording from 01–55, Inner Circle gold, or one of the Level tracks. Say which, because the next command should open that page on your machine.
What we will not do
We will not install my voice, my brain search, or my invoices. Those stay on my machines. Later we build yours.
We will not dump a hundred skills into Claude because this Mac’s Cursor only carries five, and that is the honest shelf.
When it has those two answers, it will give you one next command. Do that, then come back here and type
/aios
again. If you ask a real question about the course — not just a pick —
/aios
answers from the twenty-six lessons we wrote. When you want that in a browser tab you host, that is
/aios-coach
.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Layer 3 — Intelligence
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Layer 3 is intelligence, and most of it happens out loud and then vanishes. You had a call on Tuesday where a decision actually got made, and a client said the one sentence that explains why the deal stalled, and by Friday you cannot find it. Memory feels like a system of record because it is free. It is a terrible one.
We close that gap in three pieces, and they have to land in order.
1. Capture the meeting
I use Granola on calls. You can use Fireflies, Fathom, or a folder of transcripts you already export. I am not fussy about the vendor. I am fussy that the words land in a place the machine can see. If you have nothing, start with Granola or export last week's calls into this project. Type
/layer-3
and tell it which one you actually use. If the folder is empty, we write the smallest capture path. If you are halfway, we do not rip out what is there.
2. A brief you will actually read
Collection is not thinking. The brief is the "so what". It has to sit where you will see it — a file in this project, not a seventh tab you will never open. The rule is simple and it is the whole game: the brief cannot synthesise what it cannot see. Capture first, then the brief.
3. Something always-on in your pocket
Grok Bot is the always-on. Call 54 was the operating note: own computer, phone, receipts can run at 04:00, and coding stays in a coding harness. Hermes is the tinkery path if you like building the bot. We do not install OpenClaw.
If you want the specialist templates, Useful Resources already has that post — you build a specialist once, you share a pattern, secrets stay out. That is the walk from the community call. Type
/layer-3
and say if you want the pocket as well.
The research tools sit on this plate too
Reading the live web, pulling a podcast transcript, searching Reddit or papers — that is still intelligence. It is not a separate course. After this lesson you type
/aios
and you pick:
/web-scrape
,
/podcasts
,
/transcripts
,
/deep-research
. Those modules are on the shelf. They install through Claude Code, with your keys, not a zip.
Type
/aios
when the brief would make sense to you on a Wednesday morning.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Design Brain
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
I sat with a friend and we wrote this down properly — 1,119 design fundamentals, 30 sections, and every entry has a named source. Muller-Brockmann. Rams. WCAG. Tufte. Not “make it pop”. An entry number you can argue with.
That is Design Brain, and it is in annual on purpose, because if we only put one extra thing on this course that was not already sitting in Useful Resources, this would be it. You install the corpus. The agent cites it when you build a page, a deck, a chart, a thumbnail. It does not install my taste.
What you actually get
1,119 entries you can search offline
30 sections, from first principles through type, grid, colour, accessibility, data viz, and the failure-modes checklist
Each entry: the rule, why it exists, how to apply it, a pitfall, a number where there is one, and the source
A critique mode — violation, entry number, the rule, the source, the fix
Example: body text needs 4.5:1 against its background, large text needs 3:1 — entry #690, WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3. WebAIM’s February 2026 scan of a million home pages still found low-contrast text on 83.9 percent of them.
Download Design Brain (design-brain_v1.zip)
Install the skill from that zip, or let the community plugin put it on the shelf. Take something you are actually shipping this week and ask it to critique against the corpus.
If you are on a chart, start in section 13. Graphical excellence is #496, Tufte 1983. We use that next, on the 19-chart gallery.
The command is
/design-brain
, not
/design
— Claude Code already uses that one. When you have one critique with real entry numbers on your own work, type
/aios
again.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Chart gallery
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
I kept losing a day to the same question — which charting library do we put in this product — and a list of names does not answer it, because you cannot feel the interaction, and you cannot steal the render function.
So I built the comparison I wanted. 19 live charts. 8 libraries. Dummy data. Dark and light. Filters for distribution, flow, hierarchy, ranking, real-time, relationship and trend. The code behind every card. Dependencies vendored, so it runs offline.
Download the 19-chart gallery (chart-gallery-offline_v1.zip)
This lesson is not a post to admire. Download the zip, open
chart-gallery_v1.html
in your browser, and click something.
Do this, in order
Unzip and open the gallery. Hover, zoom, scrub, open
Code
on one card.
Pick the chart you would actually ship this month.
Ask Design Brain to critique that chart against section 13. Start with #496 and #511. If the title names the variables instead of the finding, that is #534.
Choose one default. My current shortlist: ECharts 6 as the default, shadcn/Recharts when you are already in that React desk, uPlot for dense telemetry, Lightweight Charts when people need to scrub a premium series, D3 only when the chart is the product.
The same gallery is in Useful Resources as Steal my chart gallery. Annual puts it on the OS path, next to Design Brain.
Type
/design-brain
, then
/aios
, and tell it you have a chart open.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach

lessons.title: Don't take mine. Build yours.
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
There are a few things on my machines that look like magic from the outside, and they are not magic, and you cannot have the files, because they are mine. What you can have is the process, and then a skill that is yours.
Same pattern as the GrokBot templates Matt walked — you build it once, you can share the pattern, and the secrets stay out of the share.
Your voice — not mine
I have a voice skill trained on 54 community calls and then line-edited by me. That file does not leave this desk. What we give you is the builder. You point it at your recordings, your sent mail, the lines you actually rewrote. Type
/your-voice
. The public kit is
github.com/skyremote/voice-skill-builder
. You do not install
daniel-voice
.
Your memory — not my search
I can ask an old Claude or Cursor or Codex chat what we decided last week, and I get a short pack back — not a dumped transcript. That database is not a community download. Type
/your-brain
. If you already have notes in Obsidian or a folder of transcripts, we start there. We do not make you adopt my cloud.
Your invoices — not my company
I have a skill that fills a branded invoice for NavAIgate. You do not get that template. You would be invoicing as the wrong company. Type
/your-ops
. Bring one real invoice you sent this year. We componentize that, and we stop.
If a skill has my name, my register number, my call recordings, or my old chats in it, it stays here. If it is a process you can run on your material, it belongs in the community system.
Pick one of the three this week. Then type
/aios
and say which one you started.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: The shelf
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
The five plates are the path. The shelf is the menu. There is no order on this page, and there is no prize for installing all of it.
I have watched operators finish the task audit, feel the momentum, and reach for a blank file to build something that already sits on this shelf. Do not be that person. Match the shelf against the job that is still on you, take what fits, and leave the rest.
How it works today
You already installed the community plugin —
skyremote/skool-navaigate-install
— when you did Install the crew, or you clone it and run
./install.sh
. The modules are skills on that plugin. You type
/aios
, you pick, and the matching command runs in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.
Your keys live in
~/.claude/.env
. Firecrawl, Exa, Gemini, Supadata — those are yours. We do not ship mine.
What is on the shelf
Thumbnails
— four concepts from your photos, headline composited after the image.
/thumbnails
Diagrams
— D2 in plain English, render, look, iterate.
/diagrams
Web scrape
— Exa to find, Firecrawl to extract, plus Reddit, papers, Substack, X.
/web-scrape
Podcasts
— find the episode, rank it, pull the words.
/podcasts
Transcripts
— YouTube, TikTok, IG. Paid, metered.
/transcripts
Deep research
— multi-source pass, not one search box.
/deep-research
Writing style
— anti-slop on the draft. Your voice is
/your-voice
.
/writing-style
New app
— plan, then phases, sequential.
/new-app
New capability
— talk to a tool we did not ship.
/new-capability
Frontend design
— a page that does not look generated.
/frontend-design
Your AIOS coach
— a tab that already knows this course. You put it online.
/aios-coach
Design Brain, Content Coach and Hormozi are already later in this course. They are on the same
/aios
pick list.
Type

and name the job. We will not walk you through every module. We will run the one you picked.

lessons.title: Thumbnail generator
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
The thumbnail is the click. Nobody watches the edit, the script, the three hours in the booth — not until they have clicked — and they decide in less than a second. Get this wrong and the best video you have made dies in the feed.
This module takes the thumbnail off your critical path. Four concepts, side by side, in your look. You pick. You say "the second, warmer, face left." We refine. You ship.
What it actually does
You build a small catalogue of
your
photos once — wide-eyed, pointing, arms folded, mid-laugh — tagged by expression, pose and setting. When you ask for a thumbnail on a topic, we pull the photo that fits. Not my face. Not a camera-roll scroll at midnight.
Then two stages, because this is how it actually works on the machine today.
Stage 1
— the image model draws the scene. No words. Words come out misspelled if you let it write them.
Stage 2
— we composite the headline as a real text layer after. That is how it stays spelled correctly.
Four concepts fire in parallel, different compositions, same brand rules. You judge them against each other. You cannot judge a thumbnail in isolation.
What you need
A Gemini key in
~/.claude/.env
as
GEMINI_API_KEY
. Your photo catalogue. Brand colours if you have them. Thirty to forty-five minutes on the catalogue the first time, and that pays back on every video.
Type
/thumbnails
with the video topic. You should get a 2x2. The tell that it is set up: your look holds across all four.
Type
/aios
and pick the next job.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Diagram engine
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
You have spent weeks on the plates, and when someone asks how it actually works you reach for words and lose them around the third sentence. A diagram would have closed that in five seconds. The problem was never that diagrams are hard to read. It is that they were miserable to make.
This module installs D2 — a text diagram language — and then we draw in plain English. You describe the system. We write the D2, render a PNG, look at it, and fix the overlapping labels. That look-and-fix loop is the whole point. Plenty of tools can turn text into a diagram. Most of them cannot notice it is ugly.
Five starting patterns
Master overview — the five plates and what talks to what
Data pipeline — source, store, ask
Automation schedule — trigger, job, human checkpoint
Command system — harness, skill, outcome
Education or funnel — attention, lesson, install, result
No API key. D2 is free. Five to ten minutes to stand up, and most of that is the install.
Type
/diagrams
and point it at
your
AIOS, not a toy. Ask for a one-glance version for a client and an expanded one for you. When you can produce both in a few minutes, you will stop dreading the question.
Type
/aios
and pick the next one.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Firecrawl and web scrape
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Ask Claude to look something up and half the time you get a thin summary, a 403, or a page that was mostly JavaScript and came back empty. The built-in search is fine for a quick fact. It falls over the moment the page is doing anything interesting, and the modern web is doing a lot.
This is how we read the web on the machine today. Two providers, one helper.
Exa
— semantic search. You describe what you want and you get the pages that actually match, with highlights or full text when you need them.
Firecrawl
— a real headless scrape. It runs the JavaScript and hands back clean markdown. That is the one for a SPA, a docs portal, a pricing page behind Cloudflare.
Rule of thumb: Exa to find, Firecrawl to extract. If you already have the URL, go straight to scrape.
The honest cost
Firecrawl and Exa run on credits. The default tools are free. If you are occasionally checking a fact, stay on the defaults. The moment you are doing competitor research, pulling a docs section, or reading sites at scale, the defaults cost you more in wrong answers than the keys cost in credits. Both have a free tier. Prove it to yourself.
What else is on the same helper
Same skill, different sources, because that is how we actually work:
Reddit — what broke in production, what people paid

lessons.title: Podcast search
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Some of the sharpest thinking never gets written down. It gets said. An operator goes on a two-hour podcast, drops their guard, and tells you how they priced the first deal and where go-to-market broke. You will not find that in a blog post.
The problem is finding it. The episode you want is buried across Apple, Spotify, YouTube and a hundred show sites. This module gives the agent a way to find the right interviews, rank them, and pull the full transcript of the best ones.
Two nets, because podcasts live in two places
Wide net
— Exa and Firecrawl search the open web, which is how you catch Apple, Spotify and the long tail of show sites.
Deep net
— Supadata searches YouTube, where the metadata actually lives: views, duration, date. You can ask for interviews over forty minutes from the last six months.
Then we rank. View count, duration, whether the show actually interviews operators. Best three at the top, with why. Then we pull the
full
transcript, not a summary. A summary decides for you what mattered. The transcript keeps the specifics, and the specifics are why you went looking.
Supadata is paid and metered. Put
SUPADATA_API_KEY
next to your Firecrawl and Exa keys. Keep the first pass small.
Type
/podcasts
and ask for the episodes on the thing you are actually building this week. Type
/aios
when you have the words.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Writing style
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
You can spot it in a second. The em dash, then another. The word leverage doing work no human would ask it to do. Every paragraph the same height. That texture has a name now — slop — and the reason your AI produces it is simple: a language model wrote it, and left to its own devices a language model writes like a language model.
The moment a reader clocks that smell, the thinking underneath does not matter. A strategy memo that reads like a chatbot gets skimmed and binned. If you are going to put the OS in charge of any prose a human will see — and you are — you fix the writing before it leaves the building.
What it enforces
Twelve core rules: no em dashes, vary the sentence length, start with the content, kill the binary contrasts, have an opinion. A banned-word list — leverage, delve, robust, seamless, transformative, and the rest of the fingerprint. And the structural tells: hedging, dodging a plain "is", three caveats on a point that needed none, the model narrating what it is about to do.
The self-check is the point. It drafts, it grades its own draft, it rewrites the failures before you see them.
This is not my voice
This module is the editor. Your rhythm is
/your-voice
— recordings, sent mail, the lines you actually rewrote, via
skyremote/voice-skill-builder
. You do not get my voice skill. You would be writing as the wrong person.
Type
/writing-style
on a draft you are about to send. Then
/your-voice
if you have not built that yet. Type
/aios
and pick the next job.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Build a new app
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
You have a design and the itch to build, so you point Claude at the mockup and say build this. Forty minutes later you have a beautiful login page, half a database, an API that contradicts the frontend, and no idea what is next. The model did not fail. You asked an agent to hold an entire application in its head and improvise. That never holds up.
This module is the scoping step. You hand it the design — Pencil, Figma, a screenshot, a sketch — and a sentence about what the app is for. It writes a plan file: stack, data shape, auth, pages, and the build sliced into phases you can actually ship one at a time. The plan is the output. Not code.
Phases are the whole game
An app of any real size is too big for one agent run. The model loses the thread. So we never ask it to build everything at once. Each phase is one honest session — database, then auth, then the core views. You generate a plan per phase, you open a fresh session per plan, you build phase 1 to completion before phase 2.
It is tempting to fire all seven sessions at once. Resist it. Later phases assume earlier ones exist. Sequential is slower by an hour and saves a day.
There is no
/prime
. Context is
/layer-1
and the files already in the folder. Type
/new-app
, hand it the design, and do not skip the plan file. Type
/aios
when phase 1 actually runs.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Create your own integration
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Sooner or later you hit the edge of the shelf. Content is covered, the brief is running, and then the business asks for HubSpot, or an internal API that only exists inside your company. There is no module for that, and there never will be, because it is yours.
Most people stop there and assume a new integration means becoming a developer. It does not. This skill walks you through creating the next capability — a standing piece of plumbing the OS can reach for, not a one-off script that rots in a folder.
Four steps, in order
Interrogate.
What data do you want out, where does it live, what authenticates you, how often. Most failed integrations fail here, in the vagueness.
Find the surface.
Official API, unofficial, CLI, or scrape. Pick the one least likely to break in three weeks.
Build the wiring.
A
SKILL.md
and the smallest helper. Keys in
~/.claude/.env
under your names. Nothing runs you have not seen.
Install it.
Into your skills folder, the same way the rest of this course landed.
Start with something you can verify in under a minute — the last ten items on a public feed. Then the CRM link. The first one teaches you the loop. The second one is the same conversation with higher stakes.
Type
/new-capability
and describe the gap. Type
/aios
when you can repeat the command.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Frontend design
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
A default model page is obvious from across the room. Same card grid, same inter font, same purple gradient, same empty state that says get started. If you are going to ship an interface a client will keep, you have to choose it.
This module is that pass. You lock type, colour and layout before you draw, you build in the stack you already use, and if Design Brain is on the machine we critique against the corpus — contrast, type size, grid — with entry numbers you can argue with. Not "make it pop".
If you are on a chart, start in Design Brain section 13 and use the gallery we already have. Do not invent a nineteenth chart type.
Type
/frontend-design
with the page you are actually shipping this week. Type
/design-brain
if you have not installed the corpus yet. Type
/aios
when the page would survive a screenshot.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type

— Daniel

lessons.title: Deep research
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
One search box is not research. You get the first page of whoever paid for it, and you call it done. This module is the pass we actually run when the question is "research this properly".
Scope the question in one sentence you agree with. Recon each source as hot, warm or cold — web, Reddit, papers, Substack, YouTube if you asked. Run the live ones. Exa to find, Firecrawl to extract. Academic is keyless. Reddit through Composio if you have it. Supadata only when you want the video evidence, because it is paid. Then a critic pass: recency, source type, specificity, independence. Then a synthesis with confidence labels and quotes, not a flatten.
Same helper as
/web-scrape
. Same keys in
~/.claude/.env
. Type
/deep-research
with the question you would actually pay to have answered. Type
/aios
when the synthesis has sources you can click.
When you want this in a tab of your own, type
/aios-coach
. You build it, you put it online, your key. It already knows this course. It is not on navaigate.dev yet.
— Daniel

lessons.title: Transcripts
lessons.text:
Written by Daniel Wright · NavAIgate
Listen to this lesson in my voice
Sometimes you do not want a search. You have the URL. You want the words — the YouTube talk, the TikTok, the Instagram live, the file sitting on the machine. That is this module.
